newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines worried again by Thailand's woes.
newsitem.headline: Philippines worried again by Thailand's woes.

text.p: Philippine authorities on Thursday reacted with alarm to a possible fallout of Thailand's woes on the peso and moved quickly to raise interest rates, the second time they have done so in a month.
The Central Bank had cut its overnight rates in the morning by 0.25 percentage points to 14.75 percent.
But within hours the lending rate was restored to 15 percent as news came in that the Thai baht was under pressure following the resignation of finance minister Amnuay Virawan.
The Central Bank reinforced its action by selling dollars heavily. Some traders estimated the bank may have sold up to $200 million at 26.379 and 26.380.
Last month, the Central Bank had reacted to Thailand's financial troubles by raising rates to a two-year high of 20 percent. The baht's weakening then had put pressure on several Asian currencies.
Foreign exchange traders in Manila said it was difficult to predict which way the rates would move in the next few days.

"It ( the Central Bank's key rate) can go either way. It can go back to the 13 percent level if the currency market stabilises. Or they can bring it up to 20 percent," said Deutsche Bank treasurer Enrico Cruz.
Some bankers believed the Central Bank would not raise it again to 20 percent as the Philippine stock market had performed strongly on Thursday. The main index rose almost three percent.
"I suppose it's a strong signal already that the Philippine market has reasserted itself," said Antonio Agcaoili, treasurer of Banco Santander.
"The investors may have realised we're totally different from Thailand," one analyst said.
"Fundamentally, there's no reason for us to be compared to Thailand but unfortunately because of so many similarities we're always being linked to Thailand," Deutsche Bank's Cruz said.
During Thailand's crisis last month, the Philippines found out much to its distaste that it was being compared to Thailand.
Property as well as banking stocks were battered on fears the Philippines may imitate Thailand where an overheated real estate market hurt the banking industry.
Since then those fears had died down and Manila's property stocks had just begun to recover this week.
